theory.intro: A ratio is in **simplest form** when its parts are whole numbers sharing no common factor other than $1$. Simplify by dividing **every** part by their highest common factor (HCF) — the same move as simplifying a fraction. Dividing every part by the same number gives an equivalent ratio, so the comparison is unchanged.
facts: $4:5$ is already in simplest form, because its only common factor is $1$.
Ratios with three parts simplify the same way — divide every part by the HCF of all three.
Dividing by a common factor that is not the highest leaves the ratio only partly simplified, e.g. $12:18=6:9$ still has a common factor of $3$.
steps: Find the highest common factor (HCF) of all the parts.
Divide every part by the HCF.
Check the new parts share no common factor other than $1$.

foundation.solution_text:
$4:5$
The only common factor of $4$ and $5$ is $1$, so $4:5$ is already in simplest form.

development.question_text: Kim was absent from school on $8$ of the $44$ school days in Term $1$. Write the ratio of days absent to days present in simplest form.
A netball squad has $18$ players, of whom $12$ are in Year $8$. Write the ratio of Year $8$ players to the rest of the squad in simplest form.

mastery.question_text: Simplify $120:300$ and simplify $\frac{120}{300}$. What is the same about the two methods?
mastery.solution_text:
$120:300=(120\div60):(300\div60)=2:5$
$\dfrac{120}{300}=\dfrac{120\div60}{300\div60}=\dfrac{2}{5}$
Both divide the two numbers by their HCF, $60$; a ratio and a fraction are simplified in exactly the same way.

mastery.question_text: Show that $16:24$ and $30:45$ describe the same comparison.
mastery.solution_text:
$16:24=(16\div8):(24\div8)=2:3$
$30:45=(30\div15):(45\div15)=2:3$
Both have simplest form $2:3$, so they describe the same comparison.
